key_insight: PG-KINN combines a Kolmogorov-Arnold Network trial space with a Petrov-Galerkin weak form, reducing derivative order and improving physics-informed PDE solving beyond standard MLP and strong-form KAN approaches.
engineering_relevance: This offers a more stable and interpretable neural solver for forward and inverse PDEs in computational mechanics, especially for nonlinear, non-self-adjoint, and geometry-complex problems.
method: KAN is used as the trial solution network with spline-based activations.
An independent compactly supported piecewise-polynomial test space enforces weak residuals element-wise.
Gauss-Legendre quadrature and integration by parts lower differentiation demands and improve conditioning.
evidence_signal: The paper reports benchmark gains across crack singularities, stress concentration, Neo-Hookean hyperelasticity, inverse parameter identification in heterogeneous media, and complex geometries, outperforming MLP baselines and prior KAN-based formulations.
watch_item: Performance depends on careful test-space design and quadrature accuracy, and the method may be more implementation-heavy than standard strong-form PINNs.
paper_title: PG-KINN: A Physics-Informed Petrov-Galerkin Kolmogorov-Arnold Network for Solving Forward and Inverse PDEs
